question: How do thermal properties and entrainer recovery configurations impact the economic feasibility of ionic liquid-based extractive distillation systems?
answer: The thermal properties and entrainer recovery configurations significantly impact the economic feasibility of ionic liquid (IL)-based extractive distillation systems. While ILs reduce costs in the extractive distillation column, their high boiling points and low thermal stability necessitate expensive vacuum systems, often offsetting savings. For example, in acetone/methanol separation, a two-flash-drum configuration with [MMIM][DMP] achieves only a 10.07% total annual cost (TAC) reduction due to vacuum compressor expenses. In IPA dehydration, high-purity cases (99.9999 mol%) using [EMIM][OAC] require impractical vacuum levels, making ILs 20.07% costlier than conventional entrainers. Lower-purity cases (99.99 mol%) show modest savings (8.36% TAC) with a one-flash-drum-one-stripping-column configuration, but only if most product separation occurs in the first flash. Thus, IL feasibility hinges on balancing thermal stability, vacuum requirements, and recovery configuration efficiency.

The paper investigates the use of ionic liquids (ILs) as entrainers for the separation of azeotropic mixtures in extractive distillation processes. It rigorously develops and optimizes design flowsheets for two systems, compares these with conventional processes using industrial entrainers, and assesses the economic feasibility and drawbacks of IL-based systems, including the need for high vacuum conditions due to the thermal properties of ILs.
